source.title: USDA NASS — Citrus Fruits 2024 Summary (August 2024)
source.note: Orange — yield_kg_ha (US): 18,000 kg/ha, US national average, all oranges. NASS utilized production ÷ bearing acreage: 2019-20 5,254k tons/503,700 ac; 2020-21 4,388k/491,700; 2021-22 3,426k/460,800; 2022-23 2,544k/420,900; 2023-24 2,758k/372,100 (2019-20 and 2020-21 from Citrus Fruits 2022 Summary, cfrt0922; rest from 2024 Summary). Per-season yield = short tons/acre × 907.185 kg ÷ 0.404686 ha = 23,383; 20,005; 16,667; 13,549; 16,615 kg/ha; 5-season mean 18,044 kg/ha, rounded. Tons used directly, so no box-weight conversion needed (FL 90 lb, CA 80 lb boxes already applied by NASS). Florida greening and hurricanes depress recent yields; utilized-production basis slightly below total production.

source.note: Orange — chlorpyrifos: 0.45 kg/ha; malathion: 0.35 kg/ha; imidacloprid: 0.25 kg/ha; mancozeb: 0.85 kg/ha; carbaryl: 0.60 kg/ha. Total 2.50 kg/ha, matching the aggregate in plants.json. Based on USDA NASS 2023 Fruits survey (covering Florida and California citrus production). Chlorpyrifos used for citrus psyllid and mite control; malathion for Mediterranean fruit fly management programs; imidacloprid for Asian citrus psyllid (HLB vector) suppression; mancozeb for citrus scab and brown rot fungal diseases; carbaryl for fruit thinning and secondary insect control. Confidence 2 for all compounds — NASS covers citrus in the Fruits survey but survey frequency is biennial and citrus coverage is less comprehensive than major field crops.
